title: Rollout simulation playground: traffic twists & escape scenarios (wip)
body:
Purpose
Quick sandbox for running 'what-if' rehearsals of staged rollouts, canaries and A/B windows against realistic traffic perturbations. This is an engineering+product playground: not a final runbook but a practical lab where we (1) codify typical failure modes, (2) test detection rules, and (3) surface recovery/escape paths that fit our existing console and guardrails.

Scope and intent
- Focus: short-lived canaries, microreleases, and AB lifts for LLM features (rerankers, rewriters, tokenizer variants).
- Outcomes: a catalog of simulated perturbations, expected metric signatures, guardrail thresholds that minimize cost-to-detect, and verified escape maneuvers (traffic switch, roll-forward degrade, model fallback).
- Audience: rollout stewards, SREs, product managers, and the activation conductor.

Quick primer: why simulate?
- Live traffic is noisy — early alarms are often false positives. Simulation helps us measure false alarm rates vs time-to-detect.
- We can rehearse coordination steps (who blinds, who cuts, who notifies) without impacting customers.
- Simulations let us tune cohort sizes, statistical windows, and metric smoothing so that runbook thresholds are actionable.

Core knobs in the playground
- Canary slice size: 0.5%, 1%, 5%
- Traffic burst profiles: diurnal baseline, sudden 3x burst, sustained 30% increase over 10 mins
- Error injection: latency spikes (+200–1500ms), p50/p95 token generation increases, hallucination increase simulated via label flips in synthetic prompt sets
- Model fallback: route to smaller quantized model or to previous model variant
- TTL for KV-caches / cold-KV cache penalty (simulate cold cache on rollout)
- Synthetic user personas: search-heavy, reranking-heavy, long-context users
- Weighting windows: 1/5/15/60 minute aggregation, exponential decay vs sliding-window mean

Perturbation catalog (samples)
1) Cold-kv+latency spike: instant 80% of slice sees kv-miss; p95 latency jumps from 120ms to 900ms for 6 minutes; traffic returns to normal. Expected signals: sudden p95 jump, increase in queue length, downstream downstream-retries. Recovery: auto-fallback to cached responses for 30s while we shift traffic.
2) Semantic drift (quality): inject 20% of prompts with adversarial inputs that cause a known hallucination mode. Signals: sharp rise in negative feedback metric and manual rejections, but latency unchanged. Recovery: roll back model variant, engage human-review cohort and increase exposure gating.
3) Amplified noise during holiday burst: baseline qps x3; even small error rates cause visible user impact. Signals: error budget consumption, cost spikes. Recovery: aggressive throttling + prioritize premium routes; bring dedicated capacity to bear.
4) AB interference: concurrent AB on personalization layer leads to cross-contamination of user buckets (leakage). Signals: ab metric dilution, cohort drift across assignments. Recovery: freeze new AB assignments, run cohort rehash, diag assignment service.

Metrics we bake into the sim
- Latency p50/p95/p99 (tokens and end-to-end)
- Token-cost per request (avg, 90th)
- User-visible degradation signal: human-rating or internal QA score (simulated labels)
- Traffic-levels: qps, concurrency, request size distribution
- Service health: 5xx rate, retries per request, queue latency
- SLO burn rate (computed per slice)

Detection heuristics to test
- Multi-metric fusion: semantic-quality signal must move AND token-cost delta > threshold before triggering rollback. Goal: reduce false positives from quality-only jitter.
- Symmetric drift guards: require both upward drift in p95 latency and concurrent increase in retry traffic to trigger auto-fallback.
- Minimum sample requirement: alerts only when sample count > 200 requests in window (prevents alarm on tiny slices).
- Rate-of-change heuristics: prefer relative % change over absolute deltas for metrics that scale with traffic.

Escape maneuvers (ranked)
1) Soft-revert: shift the slice back to previous model variant by 100% for that cohort for 5 minutes, keep telemetry parallel.
2) Degrade-mode: switch to fast low-cost model variant (lower quality, lower latency) for non-critical routes.
3) Throttle: reduce traffic allocation to canary to 0.1% and wait for stabilization.
4) Circuit-break and reroute: fallback to synchronous cached responses for known queries.
5) Emergency full reversion (manual): cut traffic entirely and open incident channel.

Coordination script (playbook rehearsal)
- T-minus: +0 initiation. Steward announces rehearsal in #rollout-rehearsals.
- +1m: simulate traffic perturbation in isolated sandbox (no live customers). Notify SRE and observability lead.
- +3m: run automated detector pipelines and surface generated alerts into the simulation dashboard.
- +5–10m: practice escape with traffic switch and record timings (how fast did p95 return to baseline?).
- +15m: retrospective notes written into this doc and linked_confluence.

Run experiments we want to capture (examples)
- What is the false-positive rate for the semantic-quality detector at different smoothing windows? (run 200 sims per window)
- At what canary size does latency signal reliably surface within 5 minutes under 3x burst? (test: 0.5%, 1%, 5%)
- How often does cache-cold penalty cause spurious reverts? Can we improve by warming strategy?
- Cost: measure token-cost delta for each escape maneuver to estimate ops cost for rolling forward vs reverting.

Instrumentation requirements
- Replayable synthetic traffic generator that can: play user persona mix, inject adversarial prompts, and manipulate qps patterns. (repo: rollout-sim, see linked PR)
- Sandbox metrics pipeline: mirrors production aggregator but with separate tags and higher resolution (1s).
- Dashboard templates: comparison view of baseline vs canary slice with annotated events.
- Annotated alert payloads that include: recent telemetry snapshot, traffic profile, cohort list, and suggested escape maneuvers.

Open questions / TODOs
- Should we make simulated traffic use real production prompt distributions (privacy implications)? (Priya to consult security)
- What guardrail thresholds are acceptable for self-healing vs manual intervention? Rough target: automatic actions only for p95 latency > 2x baseline AND SLO burn > 0.3 in window. Need validation.
- Decide owner for rehearsal cadence (weekly vs sprint-based). Proposal: weekly small rehearsals, monthly full-choreography.
- Add a synthetic 'human-in-loop' check: for semantic-quality drift, require at least one human-review before full automatic revert. Trade-offs?

Lab notes (initial runs)
- 2025-02-20: cold-kv sim (0.5% slice) -> p95 spike detected at 2m, soft-revert restored p95 to baseline in 40s. False alarm rate low with min-sample 200.
- 2025-02-27: semantic-drift sim (1% slice) -> quality detector flagged at 6m; because human-review gate enabled no auto-revert; manual rollback executed at +9m. Action: add faster QA quick-scan to reduce manual step time.

References and related docs
- rollout orchestration playbooks (confluence link in linked_artifacts)
- rollout-sim repo (linked PR)
- historical incident notes: incident-2024-11-model-rollback (Confluence)

Appendix: quick checklist for running a rehearsal
- Reserve slot and announce in #rollout-rehearsals
- Pick slice size and persona mix
- Ensure sandbox metrics pipeline is up and dashboard pinned
- Run sim and time detection/escape steps with stopwatch
- Capture logs, screenshots, and write retrospective entries

Bottom line
This doc is a living lab. The goal is to turn guesswork into measured trade-offs: we want predictable time-to-detect, manageable false alarms, and escape paths that map to low-cost, low-regret operations. Use this playground to stress the playbooks before we wire any automation into production.
